rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: A Boston landlord who serves a Notice to Quit or a notice that your lease will not be renewed must give you a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time and send a copy to the Office of Housing Stability. If you do not get it, report the violation to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity (617-635-2500 or 311); the eviction is not halted, but the landlord can be fined.

coverage.summary: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of any unit in Boston, except residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities or health facilities
Residences in non-profit facilities providing short-term substance abuse treatment

rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse. Requirements cannot be waived by lease.
rules.penalty: Enforced by Inspectional Services Department: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.quoted_span: The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.
rules.conflict_note: Notice requirement only; Boston, MA has no just-cause eviction law.

notes: Official city FAQ summarizing the Housing Stability Notification Act. Only rule is a notice-of-rights requirement on termination; recorded under just_cause_eviction as a notice requirement per instructions. Citation taken from the FAQ's reference to 'Sec. 10-11.7', which appears to be the HSNA section; exact codification should be verified.
